spec.name: carry_chain_roundrobin_1
spec.limitations: Expected failure mode: (1) the key is only 32 bits, so exhaustive key search costs at most 2^32 program evaluations for any buffer; (2) chaining propagates only forward and the key schedule is round-robin by byte position, so ciphertext byte 0 is a bijection of plaintext byte 0 and key byte K0 alone; one known plaintext/ciphertext pair therefore allows recovering K0 in at most 256 trials, then K1, K2, K3 from bytes 1..3 in at most 256 trials each (about 2^10 work total). The construction is a toy specimen with no proven strength and no claimed resistance to linear, differential, algebraic or slide attacks.
spec.math: For an L-byte buffer b with key K=(k0,k1,k2,k3) and per-position key byte k(i)=K[i mod 4], each step is a bijection: Xk: b_i<-b_i xor k(i); Ak: b_i<-(b_i+k(i)) mod 256; Rr: b_i<-rotl8(b_i,r); C+: b_i<-(b_i+b_{i-1}) mod 256 with b_{-1}=0 (cumulative sum, inverse b_i<-b_i-b_{i-1}); Cx: b_i<-b_i xor b_{i-1} with b_{-1}=0 (inverse b_i<-b_i xor b_{i-1} applied left to right); Xc: b_i<-b_i xor c; Ac: b_i<-(b_i+c) mod 256. The program computes E = R7 . Xk . Ak . R5 . Cx . A151 . X90 . C+ . R3 . Ak . Xk (rightmost applied first). Decryption applies the inverse of each step in reverse order, using the same key bytes: R(-7), Xk, Ak(-k(i)), R(-5), Cx^{-1}, A(-151), X90, C+^{-1}, R(-3), Ak(-k(i)), Xk. Carries in Ak and C+ make the map non-affine over GF(2) in key and data.
spec.assumptions: Assumed engine semantics: the four key bytes are assigned round-robin by buffer byte position; operands of xor_key/add_key are ignored placeholders; operands of chain_add/chain_xor are ignored; chain steps use an implicit zero predecessor and work in place left to right; all arithmetic is modulo 256 on 8-bit bytes and buffer length is fixed and known to both sides; memory is zeroed in the same convention on decryption.
